newsitem.title: DUBAI: GOLF-CARTER RECOVERING AFTER BRAIN OPERATION.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-CARTER RECOVERING AFTER BRAIN OPERATION.

text.p: English golfer David Carter was recovering on Thursday following an emergency brain operation in a Dubai hospital on Tuesday night.
A spokeswoman at the Rashid Hospital where he had the surgery to remove fluid from his brain said he was "doing fine" and added that the operation was not considered serious.
She said he would be kept in hospital for another five days.
The 24-year-old Johannesburg-born golfer, who was in Dubai to play in the Desert Classic which began on Thursday, admitted to being confused when he spoke by telephone from his bed.
"I'm feeling drowsy right now. I don't know where I am or what day it is," he said. "I know I'm in Dubai but I haven't spoken to anybody about how I am. I don't even know how I got here.
His parents, who live in Chesterfield in the English Midlands, are expected to arrive here on Friday.
Carter complained of feeling unwell on Tuesday at the Emirates course and went back to his hotel where he was found unconscious by friends in his room.
He was taken to hospital where surgery was performed to remove the fluid.
Carter suffered concussion when he hit his head on a waterslide two weeks ago while in South Africa for a tournament.
"I remember on Tuesday getting up and going to the course and not feeling well there. Then I don't remember anything until I woke up in hospital," he said.
Carter finished 33rd on the European Order of Merit last year with second and third place finishes early last season. He won the Indian PGA title late in the year.
